reviewed_by: Codex manual annotation of the local USPSTF recommendation text before E5 outputs
policy: Directions mean partial relevance, not full population transport or entailment. No-net-benefit and nonsignificance are not causal equivalence. Missing direction hints are reported separately, never silently counted as neutral agreement.

items.text: USPSTF recommends against initiating low-dose aspirin for primary prevention at age 60 or older; recommendation Grade D.
Moderate-certainty assessment: initiation at 60 or older has no net benefit.
Pooled nonfatal myocardial infarction OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.80–0.96; not restricted to adults 60+.
Pooled nonfatal ischemic stroke OR 0.88, CI 0.78–1.00, P=.046; not restricted to adults 60+.
No statistically significant cardiovascular mortality effect; this is not evidence of true zero.
Major GI bleeding increased: OR 1.58, CI 1.38–1.80; fatal/nonfatal composition and exact extracranial endpoint remain to check.
Fatal hemorrhagic stroke did not significantly increase; fatal GI bleeding remains uncertain because of sparse/inconsistent reports.
Relative bleeding effects show no clear age interaction, while absolute bleeding harm increases with age, particularly 60+.
Lifetime model at 60–69 gives QALYs slightly negative to positive and generally negative life-years; at 70–79 both are negative across essentially all modelled risks.
